The suit chooser’s picked suit

First the suit chooser as it ships. Then the picked suit as a dialog’s white card, with the card’s white, the line round it and its soft lift, as the Settings dialog draws its white cards. Version 2 has no lines between the suits. Versions 3a to 3e put a darker paper under them, one for each darker paper the site uses. The suits stand in the site’s order, clubs, diamonds, spades and hearts, as every suit chooser on the site draws them. The white card’s border is a step darker than the dialog’s line, as you asked. The Border switch steps it through the site’s darker lines. Tap a suit to move the pick. Every piece is drawn by the site’s own stylesheet.

What to look for

Today the picked suit sits on the empty rating star, a darker warm grey with a dark edge. A white card on the chooser’s paper is much quieter, since the paper is almost white. Its edge carries most of the mark, so the Border switch matters most on the light papers. The darker the paper, the more the white card stands out by itself.

On each darker paper a suit under the pointer takes the hover that paper has elsewhere on the site, and a suit you cannot pick takes the paper’s own line, so it stays as faint as today. On the quiet dark the cards’ red and black no longer read, which is why the dark papers stop there.

How it would be built

Version 1 changes the three colours of the mark in pieces.scss (--trump-pill-thumb, its ring and its lift) and nothing else. The lift is written out, since the card’s own --lift-card token is declared for dialogs only. Version 2 also drops the line between the suits. Versions 3a to 3e also set the chooser’s paper, its hover and the faded suit’s colour. The rules are at the bottom of chooser-lab-parts/lab.css.

Round 8 of the second bug hunt asked the same question on 1 Oct (its lab’s page R8-SUIT-BAND, still unanswered), with pictures from the dev site. Its V1 is version 3a here with today’s smaller lift.
